newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico awards Merida III power plant.
newsitem.headline: Mexico awards Merida III power plant.

text.p: Mexico awarded the bid to build, operate and transfer the Merida III thermoelectric plant to AES Corp, Nichimen Corp and Grupo Hermes, the Federal Electricity Commission said in a statement on Thursday.
AES Corp is a power company that generates, sells or markets electricity in more than 35 countries. Nichimen is a Japanese conglomerate. Grupo Hermes is a private Mexican company.

The CFE statement did not release the amount of the winning bid to operate the 440 Mw plant, scheduled to come on line in 2000. Construction of the plant is expected to cost at least $450 million, the CFE has said.

CFE head Rogelio Gasco Neri said the plant represents the largest energy project in Mexico to be wholly built and operated by the private sector. He said 14 other energy projects will be auctioned off during the current administration of President Ernesto Zedillo.
The companies beat out other bidders including General Electric Co, Mitsubishi Electric Corp, Itochu Corp, Enron Corp, Marubeni Corp, and Mexican firms Empresas ICA and Tribasa.
